scenes.voice: Can you spot the duplicate? Easy. Now do it for one hundred thousand numbers, fast.
NeetCode one fifty, Part one: Contains Duplicate. Given an array, return true if any number appears twice, and false if every number is unique.

scenes.label: brute force
scenes.voice: Brute force: compare every number with every other number. It works, but it takes O of n squared time. With one hundred thousand numbers, that's billions of checks.

scenes.label: better
scenes.voice: Better: sort the array first. Duplicates end up next to each other, so you only compare neighbours. That brings it down to O of n log n.

scenes.label: the one-liner
scenes.voice: There's also a one-liner: turn the array into a set and compare the lengths. A set drops duplicates, so if the length shrinks, there was a repeat. It's O of n, but it always processes the whole array. Even if the duplicate is right at the start, it still goes through all one hundred thousand numbers.

scenes.label: optimal
scenes.voice: The optimal version fixes that with a hash set and an early exit. Go through the array one number at a time. If the number is already in the set, return true immediately. If not, add it. It's still O of n in the worst case, but it stops the moment it finds a duplicate.
